lines.trans: He does not run the whole thing alone—it looks like there are junior kids following behind.
Father, I am actually one of those juniors following behind.
Sometime bring the male cast members over and film an episode visiting that clinic.
You have to take good care of urological health while you are young!
How gross!
Why are you talking on the phone right here—take it somewhere else!
I am the head of this household—where else am I supposed to go make a phone call?

meanings.note: 1st person plural pronoun; also used for 'my' with family, school, or workplace

examples.trans: Our team has a good atmosphere.
Let's eat lunch together tomorrow.
Did you hear about this son?
I was busy today because of son.

meanings.note: Points to a place near the listener, and in casual or brisk speech is used to call out to someone whose name you do not know. RR: geogi.

examples.trans: Hey, you there, just a moment!
How is the atmosphere there?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.trans: Her assigned producer? That pancake guy from last time?
Here the word for 'in charge, assigned' is key.

meanings.note: Hangul spelling of the English abbreviation PD, widely used in Korean broadcasting.

examples.trans: Who is the PD in charge of the new program?

examples.text: 그녀는 예능 피디가 되기 위해 시험을 준비했다.
examples.trans: She prepared for the exam to become a variety PD.
I ate alone today.
I can do it well by myself too.

meanings.note: Can also function as a noun
Placed before the verb it modifies.

examples.trans: I finished all my homework.
I ate all the rice.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 그래서 요 며칠 내 뒤를 졸졸 따라다니면서 선배를 떠봐?
examples.trans: So that is why you trailed behind me like a puppy these past few days sounding out your senior?
This expression comes from 'following around while'.

meanings.note: Contraction of 아이.
Colloquially used to refer to people of the same age or younger.

examples.trans: Kids are running around and playing in the park.
That person has a really good personality.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

meanings.note: Standard polite term for one's father; takes honorific particle -께서 / -께.

examples.trans: This is my father's car.
I called my father.

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.

meanings.note: Placed before a verb to emphasize immediate action or result.
E.g., 바로 옆 ('right next to'), 바로 그 사람 ('that very person').

examples.trans: I'll start right away now.
The cafe is right in front of the school.

meanings.note: interrogative noun asking about time; combines with particles like -부터 (from)

examples.trans: When did you come to Korea?
Since when have you worked here?
Did you hear about this man?
I was busy today because of man.

meanings.note: loanword from English 'member', commonly used for regular cast members of variety shows or teams

examples.trans: A new member joined.
All our team members gathered.

examples.text: 우리 애 데려다가 이게 웬 망신이야?
examples.trans: Bringing my star out here only to embarrass her like this?

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 데리다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (bringing along and).

meanings.note: refers to something known to both speakers or near the listener

examples.trans: That movie was really fun.
What is that person's name?

examples.text: 네 매형 병원이 요새 되게 힘들다.
examples.trans: Your brother-in-law's clinic is having a really hard time lately.

examples.text: 병원 문 닫고 네 매형 백수 되게 생겼다니까.
examples.trans: The clinic is about to close and turn your brother-in-law into an unemployed man.

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.trans: It's been one year since I came to Korea.
I suddenly started feeling sleepy.

meanings.note: Written as one word (한번) when softening a suggestion or request ('why don't we...').

examples.trans: Try eating this food.
Come visit sometime when you have time.

meanings.en: to film, to shoot, to take (a photo)
meanings.note: Used for capturing photos or video.
Also means to stamp a seal or dip food into sauce.

examples.trans: Did you happen to film this just now too?
May I take a photo here?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 비뇨기 계통은 젊었을 때 잘 관리를 해줘야 돼!
examples.trans: You have to take good care of urological health while you are young!
Here the word for 'urological' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 비뇨기 계통은 젊었을 때 잘 관리를 해줘야 돼!
examples.trans: You have to take good care of urological health while you are young!
Here the word for 'system' is key.
It really is young compared to what I thought.
Especially today, it is young and nice.

meanings.note: Often used as a bound noun after -(으)ㄹ to mean 'when' or 'while'.

examples.trans: Call me when you have time.
I lived in this neighborhood when I was young.
Listen closely to what I explain.
I eat Korean food well.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 비뇨기 계통은 젊었을 때 잘 관리를 해줘야 돼!
examples.trans: You have to take good care of urological health while you are young!
Here the word for 'care, management' is key.

meanings.note: Compound of 하다 (to do) and 주다 (to give).

examples.trans: Please help me (do helping for me).
Please do this for me.

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adj).

examples.trans: How gross!
This expression comes from 'how gross!'.

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb.

examples.trans: Why are you running?
Why were you late today?

meanings.note: Often used directly without a locative particle to mean 'here'.

examples.trans: Please sit here.
Here is our office.
Did you hear about this by phone call?
I was busy today because of by phone call.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (det).

examples.text: 그럼 대신 계좌는 월급 계좌 말고 딴 걸로 좀!
examples.trans: Then at least deposit it into a different account instead of my paycheck account!
Here the word for 'another, different' is key.

meanings.note: Bound noun referring to a location.

examples.trans: I have no place to go.
I have no place to go. (2)

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.note: demonstrative determiner placed before a noun

examples.text: 이 바닥은 자기 밥그릇은 자기가 챙겨야 돼.
examples.trans: In this industry, you have to look after your own rice bowl.
This book is interesting.
I'm on my way home right now.
On weekends I usually rest at home.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adv).

examples.text: 여기가 바로 편집실이다, 앞으로 네가 가장 많은 밤을 새우게 될 곳이지.
examples.trans: This right here is the editing room—the place where you will pull the most all-nighters from now on.
Here the word for 'the most' is key.

meanings.note: Interrogative pronoun for location.

examples.trans: Where is the restroom?
Where are you right now?

meanings.note: Basic verb of motion. With the respectful ending -세요 in 안녕히 가세요, it forms the polite farewell 'Goodbye!'. RR: gada.

examples.trans: I am going home.
Go safely!
Did you hear about this you?
I was busy today because of you.

이러다.gloss: to do this, to act like this

meanings.en: to do this, to act like this
meanings.note: Contracted from 이러하다.

examples.trans: Why are you acting like this?
Please don't do this.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 당신이 이러니까 우리 며느리도 뻑하면 애를 쫓아내고 말이야!
examples.trans: Because you act like this, our daughter-in-law kicks our eldest son out at the drop of a hat too!
Here the word for 'daughter-in-law too' is key.

뻑하면.gloss: at the drop of a hat

meanings.en: at the drop of a hat
meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adv).

examples.text: 당신이 이러니까 우리 며느리도 뻑하면 애를 쫓아내고 말이야!
examples.trans: Because you act like this, our daughter-in-law kicks our eldest son out at the drop of a hat too!
Here the word for 'at the drop of a hat' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 당신이 이러니까 우리 며느리도 뻑하면 애를 쫓아내고 말이야!
examples.trans: Because you act like this, our daughter-in-law kicks our eldest son out at the drop of a hat too!
This expression comes from 'chases out and'.

meanings.note: Combines with 하다 in 말하다 (to speak, to say).

examples.trans: I don't know what you mean.
You speak Korean well.

meanings.note: used both transitively and intransitively

examples.trans: The meeting is starting soon.
I started studying Korean.

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)

meanings.note: Honorific equivalent of 있다; used in 안녕히 계세요 ('goodbye' to someone staying).

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Is the teacher inside right now?
